biomarkers.description: Concentration of free D-glucose in venous plasma following a mandatory fast of at least 8 hours.

fasting_requirements.details: Patient must have zero caloric intake for at least 8 hours prior to venous collection. Water consumption is permitted.

measurement_context.methodology: Enzymatic assay using hexokinase or glucose oxidase in plasma separated from erythrocytes within 30-60 minutes or drawn in glycolytic inhibitor tube (sodium fluoride).

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Healthy Non-Diabetic Adult Reference Cohort (Subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Lower limit in healthy non-diabetic adults can physiologically extend down to 60-65 mg/dL during prolonged fasts without pathology.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Fasting plasma glucose between 100 mg/dL and 125 mg/dL (5.6-6.9 mmol/L). Identifies patients at heightened risk for future diabetes and cardiovascular complications. Requires clinical lifestyle counseling and periodic rescreening.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026) - Chapter 2: Classification and Diagnosis of Diabetes

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Fasting plasma glucose >= 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L). In the absence of unequivocal symptomatic hyperglycemia (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss) or hyperglycemic crisis, diagnosis requires two abnormal test results either from the same sample (e.g. FPG >= 126 and HbA1c >= 6.5%) or two separate test samples collected on different days. Does not constitute an automated diagnosis on a single isolated test.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026)

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Panic Alert: Severe neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia / seizure danger (< 45 mg/dL; < 54 mg/dL represents clinically significant Level 2 hypoglycemia) or Diabetic Ketoacidosis / Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State risk (> 450 mg/dL). Warrants immediate clinical notification.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: College of American Pathologists (CAP) / Joint Commission Critical Values Standards / ADA
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: Hospital laboratory panic limits for glucose commonly range from < 40-50 mg/dL (low) and > 400-500 mg/dL (high) based on inpatient vs. outpatient population, age, and institutional alert protocols.

treatment_targets.goal_description: Preprandial capillary plasma glucose target range recommended by ADA clinical practice guidelines
treatment_targets.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care (2026) - Glycemic Goals

risk_classification_thresholds.clinical_significance: Elevated lifetime incidence of diabetes; lifestyle intervention benchmark
Confirmatory repeat testing required before formal clinical diagnosis is established

provenance.clinical_notes: Diagnostic threshold (126 mg/dL) must never be stored as or confused with standard reference interval limit (99 mg/dL). Diagnostic confirmation protocol is mandatory.

biomarkers.description: Venous plasma glucose concentration drawn at any time of day without regard to interval since last meal.

fasting_requirements.details: Obtained casually without regard to meal timing.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Healthy Non-Diabetic Adults (Expected Postprandial/Casual Physiological Range; depends on carbohydrate intake and interval since meal)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry and Molecular Diagnostics / MedlinePlus
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Clinical note: 70-139 mg/dL represents expected casual postprandial glucose in non-diabetic adults; it is NOT a universal reference interval because casual glucose fluctuates dynamically with meal composition, gastric emptying, and elapsed hours post-ingestion.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Diabetes Mellitus Diagnostic Criterion (Random Glucose with Unequivocal Symptoms)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: In an individual presenting with classic symptoms of hyperglycemia (polyuria, polydipsia, unexplained weight loss) or hyperglycemic crisis, a random plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) establishes the diagnosis of diabetes without requiring repeat testing. In an asymptomatic individual, an isolated random glucose >= 200 mg/dL does NOT establish a diagnosis and mandates formal confirmatory testing (fasting plasma glucose or HbA1c on a separate sample).
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026) - Chapter 2: Classification and Diagnosis of Diabetes

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent alert: Life-threatening neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic crisis (> 450 mg/dL)
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: CAP Critical Values / Joint Commission Standards
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: Panic alert limits for random glucose depend on institutional laboratory SOP and clinical setting (ICU vs. ambulatory).

treatment_targets.goal_description: Peak postprandial capillary plasma glucose clinical target
treatment_targets.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026) - Glycemic Targets

provenance.primary_document_title: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026: Classification and Diagnosis of Diabetes
provenance.clinical_notes: Symptom status must be clinically verified prior to applying random glucose diagnostic rule. 70-139 mg/dL is an expected physiological postprandial finding, not a rigid universal reference interval.

loinc_details.method_type: HPLC, immunoassay, or capillary electrophoresis standardized to NGSP/DCCT

biomarkers.description: Ratio of beta-N-1-deoxyfructosyl hemoglobin to total hemoglobin; provides a 2-3 month weighted biological average of erythrocyte glycemic exposure.

fasting_requirements.details: HbA1c reflects chronic erythrocyte lifespan exposure; acute fasting status has zero impact on measurement.

measurement_context.methodology: Must be performed using a method certified by the National Glycohemoglobin Standardization Program (NGSP) and standardized to the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) reference assay.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Healthy Non-Diabetic Adult Cohort (Subject to NGSP assay alignment and local laboratory platform verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026) / NGSP Standards
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Assay must be NGSP certified. Values may trend slightly higher with advancing age in healthy non-diabetic elderly.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: HbA1c 5.7% to 6.4% (39-47 mmol/mol). Identifies increased risk for development of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Warrants structured lifestyle intervention.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026)

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: HbA1c >= 6.5% (48 mmol/mol). In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, requires two abnormal test results from the same sample or two separate samples. Important clinical limitation: In the presence of conditions that alter erythrocyte turnover (e.g. hemolytic anemia, sickle cell disease, pregnancy in 2nd/3rd trimester, hemodialysis, recent blood transfusion), HbA1c is unreliable and plasma blood glucose criteria must be used exclusively.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2026)

treatment_targets.target_population: Non-Pregnant Adults with Diagnosed Diabetes (General Benchmark)
treatment_targets.goal_description: General clinical recommendation: target HbA1c < 7.0% (53 mmol/mol) to reduce microvascular complications. Target may be adjusted to < 6.5% or < 8.0% based on patient age, comorbidity, and hypoglycemia risk per physician judgment.
treatment_targets.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care (2026) - Chapter 6: Glycemic Targets

risk_classification_thresholds.clinical_significance: Lifestyle intervention and annual monitoring recommended
Confirmatory repeat testing required before formal diagnosis

provenance.primary_source_organization: American Diabetes Association / National Glycohemoglobin Standardization Program (NGSP)
provenance.clinical_notes: Assay invalid in altered erythrocyte turnover states (hemolytic anemia, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, pregnancy). Inconclusive when variant hemoglobins cause assay interference.
